material_findings.finding: Onboarding promises no outbound network requests or storage/transmission beyond conversation. Bundled fetch_jd_from_url calls urllib.request.urlopen on arbitrary http/https/file URLs. Scheme checks do not impose destination, redirect, host or size restrictions. It can open a URL and read full response into memory when invoked; avoid describing package as network-inert.
material_findings.confidence: source-confirmed; no network or file reads executed from package

material_findings.finding: resolve_path builds upload_dir / upload.name and writes bytes without basename/path canonicalization, containment, exclusive create, size limit or collision rule. A forged or path-containing filename can point outside the intended directory or replace an existing local file; Streamlit's normal UI may sanitize some names, but this directly callable helper does not enforce that boundary.
material_findings.confidence: source-confirmed missing containment; no crafted upload executed

material_findings.finding: Cached lists of resume, cover letter and JD paths read all records without candidate_id filtering, and the shared file picker presents those paths regardless of active candidate. Other tab views scope by active candidate, so this creates a multi-candidate privacy consistency problem on a shared local installation. This is not evidence of remote network exfiltration.
material_findings.confidence: source-confirmed SQL is unscoped; no live multi-user demonstration

material_findings.finding: The application deliberately persists candidate-linked neurodivergence disclosure strength and factors in local SQLite and optional Markdown/PDF, while SKILL onboarding claims nothing is stored beyond conversation. The user's disclosure preference is sensitive and deserves accurate explicit persistence/retention/copy/share notice and intentional saving; not evidence of a demonstrated remote leak.
material_findings.confidence: source-confirmed persistence paths; no sensitive data generated

material_findings.finding: The dashboard copies slash-command arguments to OS clipboard and logs them under ~/.brains-resume/handoffs by default, potentially retaining job/candidate/filename/brief data beyond a chat. Handoff/logging consent and retention controls are not consistently expressed in onboarding.

Pinned SKILL declares 1.4.0, Python project declares 2.2.0, README says 2.3.0 shipped. Instructions can misdescribe current functions, migration scopes and data flow; require version coherence before consumer adoption.

Installers create Python environments, install dependencies and place links/commands in the user's Claude profile. Dashboard launcher runs Streamlit on localhost. Static skill discovery/inspection is not authorization to run these scripts or change account/app settings.
BRAINS Certified Gold is the author's own ecosystem badge and does not independently attest safety, accessibility, security or privacy practices.

positive_safeguards: User-controlled neurodivergence disclosure framing and veto rules in SKILL.md.
LinkedIn ZIP parser explicitly skips third-party Connections/Invitations/Messages by file names.
Candidate-scoped SQL exists in several individual tabs, indicating intent to isolate candidate records even though global cached pickers break consistency.
JD analyzer explicitly gates persistence via a Save button in one workflow.
MIT root LICENSE covers source-author rights; publisher mark and claims remain separately considered.
